title: Read and write a CSV file
prompt: Demonstrate CSV import/export with a temporary file or in-memory text; explain encoding, column types and safe overwrite behavior.
objective: Practice file input/output with explicit acceptance criteria and a reproducible result.

starter.source_code:
sample <- read.csv(text = "item,count\npen,3\nbook,2")
write.csv(sample, file = "sample-output.csv", row.names = FALSE)

expected_output: Do not overwrite a real user file. Use a temporary working directory and verify the row count after re-import.
acceptance_criteria: The submission addresses the task and all required core concepts.
Expected behavior and an edge case are described and checked.
Input assumptions, missing-value handling and output shape are documented where relevant.
Code is readable, uses appropriate R constructs and avoids destructive/external side effects.
Any result derived from statistics includes assumptions and relevant limitations.
hints: Identify the input, output and key R concept: File input/output.
Do not overwrite a real user file. Use a temporary working directory and verify the row count after re-import.
Test a normal case, a boundary/failure case, and verify the output independently.
grading_method: Draft/static token check only. The current platform grader can check whether the submitted text contains these strings, but it cannot execute R or prove program correctness. Keep unpublished and use human review or a separately isolated R runner before enabling XP-bearing completion.
retry_policy: Allow learner retries in a reviewed course policy; this content file does not override platform retry or XP policy.
